If, within [12] months after your start date (the 'retention period'), you resign voluntarily or your employment is terminated for misconduct, you agree to repay the unearned portion of the bonus, reduced pro rata for each full month you remained employed during the retention period. No interest, fees or other charges apply. No repayment is owed if [Company] ends your employment for any other reason, including a reduction in force, or if you resign because of [Company]'s material breach.
Method of repayment. [Company] will not deduct any repayment from your wages or final pay. Any amount due will be invoiced, and you may pay it in instalments over up to [12] months without interest.

Right to consult an attorney. You have the right to consult an attorney about this Agreement, and you have at least five business days to do so before signing. If applicable law does not permit a repayment obligation for you, the repayment paragraph does not apply.

The agreement is sent at least 5 business days before the signature deadline and signed before any payment, the deferral choice is recorded, and the retention period is no more than 12 months without Total Rewards approval (never more than 24).

sections.title: Country clause library
sections.intro: Non-US hires are employed by the local entity under a local-law contract, and some US states need inserts. These blocks give what each jurisdiction's offer or contract must contain; Legal holds the full local templates.

items.text: Canada termination clause caution: in Ontario, one ESA-non-compliant sentence, including the for-cause clause, voids every termination provision (Waksdale, 2020 ONCA 391). Dufault v. Ignace (2024 ONCA 915; SCC leave denied June 2025) voided a clause over 'sole discretion ... at any time' wording, its cause definition and its benefits wording. Baker v. Van Dolder's Home Team / Li v. Wayfair (2026 ONCA 568, Aug 2026) held that 'at any time' and 'for any reason' can survive where the contract, read as a whole, repeatedly guarantees ESA minimums; watch for an SCC leave application. Use only the Legal-approved clause, avoid 'sole discretion', and never edit it for an individual offer.

Canada (Ontario / BC) termination clause [Legal-approved text; do not edit]: 'Termination without cause. [Company] may end your employment without cause by providing you with the minimum notice of termination or pay in lieu of notice, severance pay or compensation for length of service (if applicable), continuation of your benefits during the statutory notice period, and any other entitlements required by the [Employment Standards Act, 2000 (Ontario) / Employment Standards Act (British Columbia)], as amended. You agree that these statutory entitlements satisfy in full any notice or pay in lieu of notice you would otherwise be entitled to at common law. Termination for cause. [Company] may end your employment without notice or pay in lieu only in circumstances in which the employment standards legislation requires no notice or severance. Minimum standards. If the employment standards legislation requires any greater notice, payment or benefit than this agreement provides, you will receive the statutory minimum instead; nothing in this agreement is intended to provide less.'

Canada, other required clauses: 'This offer is conditional on your signing this agreement before your start date.' 'You assign to [Company] all rights in inventions and works you create in the course of your employment and waive your moral rights in them to the extent permitted by law.' 'Equity awards are governed by the plan and award agreement; unvested awards will not continue to vest during any period of notice or pay in lieu beyond the minimum period required by the employment standards legislation.'
items.detail: Signed before Day 1, or changes need fresh consideration. Equity forfeiture wording must be clear and unambiguous (Matthews). No Ontario non-compete below the C-suite (ESA s.67.2). Ontario (25+): give the new-hire information statement before Day 1.

items.text: Colorado non-compete notice [separate document, only if a non-compete or customer non-solicit is used]: 'Notice of Restrictive Covenant. The [agreement name] that [Company] is asking you to sign contains a covenant not to compete [and a covenant not to solicit customers] that could restrict your options for subsequent employment following your separation from [Company]. The covenant is in section[s] [x] of the enclosed agreement. Please sign below to confirm that you received this notice before accepting our offer.' Employee signature: __________ Date: __________
items.detail: Give it with the offer so the candidate receives it before accepting, as a separate, signed document in clear terms (C.R.S. 8-2-113(4)). The covenant is valid only for highly compensated workers ($130,014 in 2026; customer non-solicits $78,008.40), to protect trade secrets, with Colorado law and venue; non-compliant covenants carry $5,000 penalties per worker. Company default: no non-competes.

items.text: Washington noncompetition disclosure [only if a noncompete is used before 30 June 2027]: 'The terms of the noncompetition covenant [Company] will require you to sign are set out in section [x] of the enclosed [agreement name]. [Company] is disclosing these terms to you in writing before you accept this offer. The covenant is enforceable only if your annualized earnings exceed the threshold set under RCW 49.62 ($126,858.83 in 2026).'
items.detail: Written disclosure no later than initial acceptance of the offer (RCW 49.62.020); if the covenant may become enforceable later, say so. All Washington noncompetes become void on 30 June 2027 (ESHB 1155), so the default is none. The PIIA needs the RCW 49.44.140 invention notice.

items.text: North Carolina wage insert: 'Your salary will be paid [semi-monthly on the 15th and last day of each month] by direct deposit [or at [location]]. The Company's vacation/PTO and bonus policies are enclosed, including the conditions under which unused vacation or an unearned bonus is forfeited.'
items.detail: Written wages, payday and place of payment are required (G.S. 95-25.13). Have any non-compete signed with the offer, when new employment is the consideration.

items.text: Texas: use the Texas package (at-will, Texas law and venue, payday schedule, written bonus and vacation-payout terms). Any non-compete or non-solicit must be ancillary to confidential information or equity (Bus. & Com. Code 15.50); offers may not require COVID-19 vaccination (SB 7); repayments can be deducted from wages only with written authorization (Labor Code 61.018).

California: no non-compete (B&P 16600) and no non-California law or forum (LC 925). The PIIA carries the LC 2870 invention notice and the DTSA immunity notice, and non-exempt hires also get the LC 2810.5 wage notice.

Germany: particulars of employment (NachwG §2), in the German-law contract (bilingual recommended): 'Parties: [Company GmbH], [address], and [employee name], [address]. Start date: [date]. [Fixed term until [date].] Place of work: [office] [; mobile work under company policy]. Position and duties: [job title and description]. Probation: [up to 6] months, with two weeks' notice during probation. Pay: gross annual salary EUR [amount], paid in 12 monthly instalments at the end of each month by bank transfer; [overtime compensated by [time off / payment at [rate]]]; [variable pay under the [plan]]. Working time: [40] hours a week, with rest breaks and rest periods under the Working Hours Act; [flextime / shift system]; overtime may be ordered within legal limits. Annual leave: [30] working days (including the 20-day statutory minimum on a 5-day week). Training: [any employer-provided training entitlement]. Company pension: [provider name and address, if applicable]. Termination: notice periods under §622 BGB [or [x] months to month-end]; notice must be in writing with a handwritten signature (§623 BGB); an employee who wishes to challenge a dismissal must file a claim with the labour court within three weeks of receiving it (§4 KSchG). Collective and works agreements: [references / none].'

Germany timing: parties, pay and working time by day 1; start date, fixed-term end, place, duties, probation and overtime by day 7; the rest within 1 month (§2 NachwG). Text form is allowed since 2025 if the employee can store and print it and is asked to confirm receipt, with paper on request; fines up to EUR 2,000 per breach. A fixed-term clause needs wet-ink (or qualified e-signature) signatures before the start (§14(4) TzBfG); with more than 20 employees the works council must consent to the hire (§99 BetrVG); non-competes need at least 50% Karenzentschädigung (§74 HGB); invention terms follow the ArbnErfG. No US at-will or US governing-law terms.

Israel: notice of employment terms (Notice to Employee and Job Candidate Law 2002), which may be combined with the signed agreement if it covers every item: 'Employer: [Company Israel Ltd.], [address], company no. [x]. Employee: [name], ID no. [x], [address]. Start date: [date]; term: [indefinite / until [date]]. Position and main duties: [x]. Direct supervisor: [title]. Pay: total monthly salary NIS [amount], comprising base salary NIS [x] [and global overtime of NIS [x] for up to [y] overtime hours a month], paid by the [9th] of the following month. Working hours: [x] hours a week over [5] days; weekly rest day: [Saturday / other]. Social benefits: pension at [6]% employee and [6.5]% employer contributions, plus [8.33]% employer severance contributions under a Section 14 arrangement, to [fund]; study fund (keren hishtalmut) at [2.5]% employee and [7.5]% employer. Employers' organization or collective agreement: [none / name].'

Israel: deliver within 30 days of the start date and give later changes in writing. The agreement also needs the Section 14 annex, an invention assignment with an explicit waiver of royalties under Patents Law s.134, confidentiality and notice terms, and (for equity) the Section 102 trustee route. Use special-trust status or global overtime only where genuine; check minimum pension rates against the current extension order (verify).

India: appointment letter (OSH Code s.6(1)(f)), issued at joining after the offer letter: 'You are appointed as [designation] in [department] of [Company India Pvt. Ltd.] at [work location], with effect from [date of joining]. For the purposes of the labour codes you are classified as [a worker / an employee employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity / a supervisor earning above the prescribed limit]. Your annual cost to company is INR [amount], of which wages (basic pay, dearness allowance and retaining allowance) are INR [amount], not less than 50% of total remuneration, as shown in Annexure A. You will be enrolled in the Employees' Provident Fund [and ESI, if eligible] and will be eligible for gratuity under the Code on Social Security, 2020. Probation: [6] months. Working hours: [x] hours a day and [y] a week. Notice: [x] months' written notice or pay in lieu[, subject to the Industrial Relations Code for workers]. You are bound by the enclosed confidentiality and intellectual property assignment agreement and the Code of Conduct.'

India: record the worker or non-worker category accurately (it drives retrenchment compensation, standing orders and grievance rights), check whether state rules prescribe a form (verify for Karnataka and Telangana), and pay e-stamp duty on the employment agreement at execution. Post-employment non-competes are void (Contract Act s.27), and joining-bonus clawbacks must be reasonable, pro-rated liquidated damages.

China: labour contract terms (LCL Art. 17), bilingual with Chinese prevailing: 'Employer: [Company (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.], address [x], legal representative [x]. Employee: [name], ID no. [x], address [x]. Term: [fixed term of [3] years from [date] / open-ended]. Probation: [up to 6] months at not less than 80% of the agreed salary. Position and work location: [x], [city]. Working hours: [standard working hours / comprehensive or flexible system approved by the labour bureau]; rest and leave per law and the employee handbook. Remuneration: monthly salary RMB [amount], paid on the [x] day of each month [; 13th-month salary: [contractual / discretionary]]. Social insurance and housing fund: per local regulations. Labour protection, working conditions and occupational hazard protection: per law and company rules. [Confidentiality; non-compete only for senior management, senior technical and confidential staff, with monthly compensation.]'

China: sign the written contract on or before Day 1 and never later than one month after the start, or double wages accrue from month 2 for up to 11 months and an open-ended contract is deemed after a year (LCL Arts. 10, 14, 82). The accepted offer letter is itself binding. Probation is capped by term (1 month for terms under a year, 2 months for 1-3 years, 6 months for 3+ years or open-ended), and non-compete compensation must be at least 30% of prior average monthly pay.

Taiwan: employment contract terms (LSA Enforcement Rules Art. 7), with a Traditional Chinese version: 'Term: non-fixed (indefinite). Work location and duties: [x], [city]; any transfer will follow the five principles in LSA Art. 10-1. Working hours: [8] hours a day and [40] a week [, flexible start between [x] and [y]]; overtime requires prior approval and is paid under LSA Art. 24 [or taken as compensatory leave if you choose]. Wages: monthly wage NT$[amount], comprising [base salary and fixed allowances], paid on the [x] of each month; [year-end bonus: [discretionary / guaranteed [x] months]]. Leave: annual leave, holidays and other leave per the LSA and the work rules. Pension: at least 6% employer contribution to your Labor Pension individual account. Termination and severance: per the LSA and the Labor Pension Act. Safety and health, training, welfare, occupational-injury compensation, and rewards and discipline: per the work rules.'

Taiwan: don't use fixed-term contracts for ongoing roles (LSA Art. 9). Name the employer as author of works made for hire (Copyright Act Art. 11), address service-invention remuneration (Patent Act Art. 7), and make any post-employment non-compete meet LSA Art. 9-1 (in writing, at most 2 years, compensation of at least 50% of average monthly wage).

Vietnam: labour contract content (Labor Code 2019 Art. 21; Circular 10/2020), in Vietnamese (bilingual for foreigners), two originals or a registered e-contract: 'Employer: [Company Vietnam LLC], [address], represented by [name, title]. Employee: [name], date of birth [x], sex [x], residence [x], personal ID no. [x] [; work permit no. [x]]. Job and workplace: [title and duties], [address]. Term: [indefinite / definite term of [x] months, not more than 36]. Salary: VND [amount] gross per month plus allowances [list], paid by bank transfer on the [x] of each month; salary review [annually]. Working hours and rest: [8] hours a day, [40] hours a week; annual leave of [12+] days. Probation: [up to 60] days at [at least 85]% of salary [in this contract / a separate probation agreement]. Social, health and unemployment insurance: per law. Training: [x]. Protective equipment: [as required]. Annex: confidentiality, trade secrets and IP assignment (Art. 21(2)).'
items.detail: Sign before work starts; an offer letter doesn't replace the contract. E-contracts go through a licensed provider and the national platform (Decree 337/2025), and a foreign employee's contract can't outlast the work permit.

notes: Choose the template by work location and employing entity. A US at-will letter used for a Canadian, German, Israeli or Asian hire is the costliest drafting mistake in this library (e.g., uncapped common-law notice in Canada).
Offer letters give a target equity value subject to Board or Committee approval and plan terms, never a share count; grants follow the equity grant calendar (POL-27).

Repayment terms never go in the offer letter: sign-on repayment sits only in the standalone agreement, and relocation, training or immigration-cost repayment isn't used for California workers (AB 692).

Contingencies are listed, time-bound and lawful: background check after the conditional offer, I-9 within three business days of the start, export authorization only for flagged roles, and the PIIA signed by Day 1.
Every letter and PIIA includes protected-rights wording (SEC Rule 21F-17, NLRA, California Silenced No More) so that no term can be read as blocking reports to regulators.

Local contracts are signed before Day 1 almost everywhere (Canada for enforceability, Vietnam before work starts, Germany for fixed terms, China within one month at the latest); Greenhouse holds the start date until the signed copy is uploaded.
Clause library text is controlled by Legal. Recruiters fill in brackets only, and requested changes go through the deviation workflow in T-OFFER-APPROVAL.

countryNotes.us: Offer letters state at-will status, exempt or non-exempt classification and the contingencies, and the PIIA carries the DTSA immunity notice and state invention notices. Don't use non-competes in MN, ND, OK, WY or California, or in Washington from 30 June 2027, and check income thresholds in other states.
countryNotes.us-ca: Use California law and forum (LC 925), no non-compete (B&P 16600), the LC 2870 invention notice, and no repayment terms except a standalone sign-on bonus agreement that fits the AB 692 exception. Exempt pay must be at least $70,304 in 2026 ($72,384 in 2027), and non-exempt hires get the LC 2810.5 wage notice.
countryNotes.us-co: Any non-compete or customer non-solicit needs the separate signed notice before acceptance, the 2026 pay threshold ($130,014 or $78,008.40), a trade-secret purpose and Colorado law and venue (C.R.S. 8-2-113). Training-cost repayment is allowed only for non-routine training, prorated.
countryNotes.us-nc: State the promised wages and the day and place of payment in writing, and attach the PTO and bonus forfeiture policies (G.S. 95-25.13). Have non-competes signed with the offer; out-of-state forum and jury-waiver clauses are void (G.S. 22B-3, 22B-10).
countryNotes.us-tx: Use the Texas template: at-will, Texas law and venue, the payday schedule and written bonus and vacation terms, with any non-compete ancillary to confidential information or equity (Bus. & Com. Code 15.50). Repayments can be deducted from wages only with written authorization (Labor Code 61.018).
countryNotes.us-wa: Disclose any noncompete in writing by offer acceptance and meet the $126,858.83 threshold (2026); all noncompetes become void on 30 June 2027 (ESHB 1155). Exempt offers must meet $80,168.40 (2026), and the PIIA needs the RCW 49.44.140 invention notice.
countryNotes.ca: Use a Canadian contract with the Legal-approved ESA-compliant termination clause (Waksdale; Dufault; Baker, 2026 ONCA 568), IP assignment with a moral-rights waiver and Matthews-compliant equity wording, signed before the start date. Ontario non-competes are void below the C-suite, and Ontario employers with 25+ employees give the new-hire information statement before Day 1.
countryNotes.de: Issue a German-law contract that covers the NachwG particulars on the statutory timeline, with probation of up to 6 months, ArbnErfG-compliant invention terms and any non-compete only with 50% Karenzentschädigung. Fixed-term clauses need wet-ink signatures before the start, and hires need works council consent above 20 employees.
countryNotes.il: Use an Israeli-law agreement with the Section 14 annex, pension and study-fund rates, an invention assignment with an explicit s.134 waiver, and special-trust or global-overtime terms only where genuine. Deliver the statutory notice of terms within 30 days of the start date.
countryNotes.in: Issue the offer letter, then the statutory appointment letter at joining with the worker or non-worker category and a pay structure meeting the 50% 'wages' rule. Stamp the employment agreement, and don't rely on post-employment non-competes (Contract Act s.27).
countryNotes.tw: Put the Enforcement Rules Art. 7 terms in writing with a Traditional Chinese version, use indefinite-term contracts for ongoing roles, and meet LSA Art. 9-1 for any non-compete. Name the employer as author of works made for hire and address service-invention remuneration.
countryNotes.cn: Sign the Chinese or bilingual labour contract with the LCL Art. 17 terms on or before Day 1, and never later than one month, or double wages accrue. Probation must match the contract term at 80%+ pay, and non-competes are limited to senior and confidential staff with monthly compensation.
countryNotes.vn: Sign the Vietnamese (or bilingual) labour contract with the Art. 21 content and the confidentiality and IP annex before work starts. Definite terms run at most 36 months, probation for degree-level roles is at most 60 days at 85%+ pay, and a foreigner's contract can't outlast the work permit.

templates.name: Reference check guide
templates.purpose: A structured, consent-based reference call that tests the same competencies as the interview loop and produces evidence the hiring team can weigh. It keeps reference checks lawful across countries, avoids prohibited topics, and flags when a reference becomes a regulated consumer report.
templates.audience: Recruiters and hiring managers who conduct references; TA Operations and the background-check vendor for vendor-run references.
templates.when: For the preferred finalist after the final-round debrief, or after the conditional offer where Legal requires it; always completed before the start date (TA-05).
templates.owner: Talent Acquisition (guide and process); Legal (country rules and adverse decisions)

sections.title: Consent and set-up
sections.intro: No call is made until every item is complete.

items.text: The candidate has consented in writing (Greenhouse e-signature) to reference checks, naming the referees we may contact and acknowledging the candidate privacy notice.
The candidate chose the referees: 2-3 people, including at least one former manager. A current-employer reference is taken only if the candidate agrees, normally after they have accepted the offer.
No backdoor references: we don't contact anyone the candidate hasn't agreed to, including mutual connections or former colleagues found online.
Timing agreed: references for the preferred finalist only, after the final debrief [or after the conditional offer where Legal requires it], completed within 5 business days.
Each referee's identity and relationship are confirmed through a company email address, switchboard or professional profile, not only a mobile number supplied by the candidate.

References run by a third-party vendor are consumer reports in the US (investigative consumer reports when the vendor interviews people), so the FCRA disclosure, authorization and adverse action steps apply, and California needs the separate ICRAA disclosure (T-FCRA-NOTICES).
Use the same questions for every finalist for the role so that references can be compared fairly, and have one person (recruiter or hiring manager) run all of a candidate's references.
Referee name, title and company
Relationship to the candidate
items.detail: Manager / skip-level manager / peer (same or another site) / direct report / customer or partner. Aim for one former manager and one cross-site peer; for people managers, add a former direct report.

items.text: Period of working together and projects in common
items.detail: References with less than 6 months' overlap, or from more than 7 years ago, carry less weight.

items.text: Consent record and date
items.detail: Link to the candidate's signed consent listing this referee.

items.text: Avoid personal friends and relatives. If a referee's employer allows them to confirm only dates and title, thank them and ask the candidate for another referee; don't press.

Hello [Referee name], this is [your name], [title] at [Company]. [Candidate name] has applied for a [Job title] role with us and gave us your name as a reference. Is this still a good time for about 20 minutes?
[Candidate name] has consented to this call. I'll ask about your experience of working with them, and my notes go only to our hiring team.
We keep your comments confidential within our hiring process as far as the law allows. In some countries the candidate can ask to see the information we hold about them.
items.detail: Don't promise absolute confidentiality: access rights exist under the GDPR, PIPL, CCPA, Israeli privacy law and others.

items.text: Please don't share anything confidential about your company, its products or its customers. I'm only interested in how [Candidate name] worked.
Could you start by describing how you worked with [Candidate name]: your role, their role, and roughly when?

sections.title: Structured questions
sections.intro: Ask each question as written and in this order. Record specific examples, in the referee's words where possible.

items.text: What were [Candidate]'s main responsibilities, and what was the scope of their work (team size, products, sites)?
items.detail: Check that the scope matches the level we're hiring at.

items.text: How would you describe the depth of their technical expertise in [area from the role]? Where were they the person others went to?
Tell me about a difficult technical problem or bug they worked on. What was their personal contribution?
How did they work with teams in other sites, time zones or functions? Can you give me an example?
Tell me about a time something they owned went wrong or slipped. How did they respond?
How did they communicate status, risks and bad news to you and to others?
What feedback did you give them most often, and how did they act on it?
In a role like [brief description], where would they be strongest, and where would they benefit from support?
For people managers: How did they build and develop their team, and how did they handle a performance problem?
On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate their overall performance compared with others you've worked with at the same level? What would have made it a 10?
Would you work with them again, or hire them if you could? Why or why not?
Is there anything else we should know that would help them succeed here?
Probes for any answer: 'Can you give me a specific example?' 'What did [Candidate] do personally, as opposed to the team?' 'What was the result?' 'How did that compare with others at the same level?'
If answers are vague or very short: 'It sounds as though some of this may be hard to talk about. Is there anything you're not able to share, or would you prefer we move on?'
items.detail: Some employers restrict references. Accept that without drawing conclusions.

items.text: Red flag: the referee can't confirm the candidate's role, level, dates or the projects the candidate described, or describes a materially different scope.
Red flag: consistent faint praise, long pauses or a qualified answer to the 'work with them again' question, especially from a former manager. Probe once, then record what was said.
Red flag: the referee appears to be a friend or relative, seems coached, or can't give a single specific example.
Red flag: the referee suggests the candidate took, shared or offered an employer's confidential information or code. Stop that line of questioning, don't ask for details, and escalate to Legal.

One negative reference isn't decisive. Weigh it against the interview evidence and the other references; if it could change the decision, discuss it with the hiring manager and consider letting the candidate respond, without naming the referee unless they agree.
Health, disability, sick or medical leave, workers' compensation claims or accommodations; pregnancy, maternity or parental leave; family or childcare arrangements.
Age, national origin, citizenship, religion, caste, race, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, union membership or activity, political views, and (Israel) reserve duty.

Pay history, including base, bonus or equity at the referee's company. Banned in California, Colorado, Washington, BC and many other US states and cities, and the bans cover questions through third parties.

Criminal history, arrests or legal disputes, and whether the candidate filed complaints, took part in investigations, blew the whistle or sued an employer. Asking can itself be evidence of retaliation.
Confidential information about the referee's company, its products, customers or roadmaps, and requests for performance ratings or HR documents.
Thanks; that's not something we take into account. Could you tell me more about [work topic]?
items.detail: Use this if a referee volunteers protected information. Don't follow up and don't record it.

items.text: Reference summary for each referee
items.detail: Relationship and overlap; answers by question with specific examples; overall assessment against the competencies; any red flags, with the evidence. Facts and quotes, not impressions.

items.text: Overall reference outcome
items.detail: Supports hire / Supports hire with development points / Concerns requiring discussion. Recorded in the Greenhouse reference form within 1 business day of the last call.

items.text: No protected information, pay history or confidential employer information is recorded, even if the referee volunteered it.
Only the recruiter, hiring manager and approvers can see the reference form; it is kept on the TA-11 retention schedule and never filed in the personnel file.

If a vendor-run reference contributes to withdrawing a US offer, follow the FCRA pre-adverse and adverse action steps in T-FCRA-NOTICES. For recruiter-run references, Legal decides what notice to give.
Candidates may ask to see what we recorded (GDPR, PIPL, CCPA, DPDP, Israeli privacy law, Vietnam PDPL), so write every summary as if the candidate and the referee will read it.

notes: References test evidence, not reputation: the questions mirror the interview competencies so the hiring manager can compare them with the scorecards.

Consent comes first everywhere: in the US for fairness and, for vendor checks, the FCRA; under the GDPR, PIPL, PDPL, DPDP and Israeli law because contacting referees processes the candidate's personal data.
Never call a current employer without the candidate's clear agreement; an unauthorized call can cost the candidate their job and expose the company to claims.
A reference that changes a hiring decision must be documented with job-related evidence, never 'fit' or hearsay.
Keep notes factual: they can be disclosed to candidates on request and may be discoverable in litigation.
For hires from direct competitors, references also test clean-hire risk; any hint of trade-secret misuse goes to Legal, not into the debrief.

countryNotes.us: Recruiter-run references aren't regulated by the FCRA, but vendor-run references are consumer reports (investigative reports when the vendor interviews people) and need disclosure, authorization and adverse action steps. Don't ask about pay history where banned, or about disability or medical leave (ADA, FMLA).
countryNotes.us-ca: Vendor-run references need the separate ICRAA disclosure and a box to request a copy (Civ. Code 1786), and pay-history questions are banned, including through agents (LC 432.3). Truthful references are privileged (Civil Code 47(c)), and reference notes fall under CCPA access rights.
countryNotes.us-co: Colorado presumes good faith for employers who disclose job-performance information (C.R.S. 8-2-114), so former employers may say more. Don't ask about salary history, age or graduation dates, or sealed records.
countryNotes.us-nc: Accurate, good-faith references on performance and reasons for separation have qualified immunity (G.S. 1-539.12), so referees may answer more fully. Don't ask about expunged records (G.S. 15A-153).
countryNotes.us-tx: Performance references are immune unless knowingly false or reckless (Labor Code 103.003-103.004), and a truthful discharge reason may be requested; blacklisting is prohibited. Ask candidates from Texas competitors about any non-compete or non-solicit before calling their references.
countryNotes.us-wa: Good-faith performance references are immune (RCW 4.24.730), but don't ask about salary history (RCW 49.58.100), criminal history before a conditional offer or cannabis use. Recording a reference call needs the referee's consent (RCW 9.73.030).
countryNotes.ca: Get written consent and give notice of the purpose (BC PIPA; Ontario Consumer Reporting Act notice where an agency is used), and don't ask about protected grounds, including record of offences in Ontario. Quebec's Law 25 requires consent for disclosure, so referees there may decline.
countryNotes.de: References need the candidate's consent (GDPR Art. 6; BDSG §26) and must stay job-related; contacting a current employer without consent is unlawful. Ask the candidate for their written Arbeitszeugnis, and delete reference notes about 6 months after a rejection.
countryNotes.il: Contact referees only with the candidate's consent and give the Amendment 13 privacy notice; candidates may ask for their screening results. Don't ask about reserve duty, pregnancy, fertility treatment or place of residence, and keep notes factual (Prohibition of Defamation Law 1965).
countryNotes.in: Use written consent that names the referees and covers vendor verification; former employers need the ex-employee's consent to answer (SPDI Rules now, DPDP Act from May 2027). Relieving and experience letters verify dates and designation.
countryNotes.tw: Get written consent under the PDPA before contacting referees, and keep questions job-related. Former employers issue a certificate of service on request (LSA Art. 19), which confirms dates and position.
countryNotes.cn: PIPL requires the candidate's consent for reference calls and a notice covering vendors, and former employers answer only with the employee's consent. Always collect the termination certificate and ask about non-compete and confidentiality obligations, since hiring someone still bound creates joint liability (LCL Art. 91).
countryNotes.vn: References and verifications need the candidate's consent under the PDPL, and criminal-record or health information must not be sought through referees. Former employers provide working-history documents on request (Labor Code Art. 48(3)), which can replace detailed questions.

templates.name: Background check disclosure and adverse action notices
templates.purpose: The US forms and letters for background checks run through a consumer reporting agency: the stand-alone FCRA disclosure, the authorization, the pre-adverse and final adverse action letters and the California Fair Chance Act individualized assessment. With the timeline checklist and state and city variations, they keep every check and every adverse decision procedurally correct.
templates.audience: Recruiters and TA Operations (sending), Legal (assessments and adverse decisions), the background-check vendor (reports and disputes).
templates.when: After a conditional offer is accepted (TA-05): disclosure and authorization before any report is ordered; the pre-adverse and final notices only when a report may lead to withdrawing the offer.
templates.owner: Talent Acquisition Operations (forms and timeline); Legal (individualized assessment and final decision); Background-check vendor (reports and disputes)

sections.title: Stand-alone disclosure
sections.intro: Shown on its own screen or page before any other form in the vendor portal. It may contain nothing else.

items.text: DISCLOSURE REGARDING BACKGROUND INVESTIGATION. [Company] (the 'Company') may obtain information about you from a third-party consumer reporting agency for employment purposes. As a result, you may be the subject of a 'consumer report' [and an 'investigative consumer report'] prepared by [Vendor name], which may include information about your [identity, employment history, education, professional licenses, criminal history, motor vehicle record (driving roles only), credit history (only for roles where the law allows it)].

[Only if investigative consumer reports, such as vendor-run reference interviews, will be obtained:] An investigative consumer report may include information about your character, general reputation, personal characteristics and mode of living, obtained through personal interviews with people who know you, such as former employers and references. You have the right, on written request made within a reasonable time, to a complete and accurate disclosure of the nature and scope of the investigation.
items.detail: Answer any such request within 5 days (15 U.S.C. 1681d).

items.text: The consumer reporting agency is [Vendor legal name], [address], [toll-free phone], [website]. Its privacy practices are described at [link].

The disclosure must be clear and conspicuous and in a document that consists solely of the disclosure (15 U.S.C. 1681b(b)(2)(A)). Don't add liability releases, state notices, at-will acknowledgments or other extra text: courts have allowed class claims over a single extra sentence (Syed v. M-I, 9th Cir. 2017; Gilberg v. California Check Cashing Stores, 9th Cir. 2019).
Present the disclosure only after a conditional offer (the company-wide standard, which meets California, Washington and other fair-chance laws), and put state notices on separate pages.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.intro: May appear on the same screen as the disclosure only if nothing else is added; the vendor portal keeps them as separate steps.

items.text: AUTHORIZATION. I have read the Disclosure Regarding Background Investigation and 'A Summary of Your Rights Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act'. I authorize [Company] to obtain consumer reports [and investigative consumer reports] about me from [Vendor name] for employment purposes in connection with my application [and, where the law allows, during my employment].
items.detail: Delete the ongoing-employment wording unless Legal has approved periodic re-checks and the state allows them.

items.text: Full name and any other names used
items.detail: Needed for accurate record matching.

items.text: Date of birth and Social Security number
items.detail: Collected in the vendor's secure portal after the conditional offer, never by the hiring team or on the application (Colorado JAFA; age-discrimination risk).

items.text: Addresses for the last 7 years, and the education and employment history to be verified
Signature and date
items.detail: Electronic signatures are valid under the E-SIGN Act; keep the timestamp.

items.text: California applicants [and applicants in other states that require it]: [ ] Check this box to receive a free copy of any consumer report or investigative consumer report obtained about you.
items.detail: California's ICRAA disclosure (Civ. Code 1786.16) goes on its own page with the nature and scope of the investigation, the agency's contact details and privacy practices, and the right to inspect the agency's files.

sections.title: Individualized assessment (California Fair Chance Act and similar laws)
sections.intro: Complete in writing, before any pre-adverse notice, whenever a conviction may affect the decision. Legal signs it.

items.text: Conviction(s) considered
items.detail: Convictions only. Never consider arrests that didn't lead to conviction, referral to or participation in diversion, sealed, dismissed, expunged or statutorily eradicated records, juvenile records or (California) certain cannabis convictions more than 2 years old (LC 432.7, 432.8).

items.text: Nature and gravity of the offense or conduct
items.detail: The harm caused, how it relates to the job's duties, and any aggravating or mitigating circumstances.

items.text: Time since the offense and since completion of the sentence
Nature of the job held or sought
items.detail: The specific duties and setting, e.g., access to trade secrets or controlled technology, financial authority, or unsupervised access to others' property.

items.text: Evidence of rehabilitation or mitigating circumstances considered
items.detail: e.g., education or training completed, work history since the offense, references, age at the time of the offense, and anything the candidate provided.

items.text: Preliminary decision, reasons, reviewer and date
items.detail: Kept in the screening file, separate from the personnel file. California doesn't require sending the assessment to the candidate, but it may be shared.

sections.title: Pre-adverse action notice
sections.intro: Sent before any decision is final, with a copy of the report and the CFPB 'A Summary of Your Rights Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act'.

items.text: Dear [Candidate name], thank you for your interest in the [Job title] position. As part of our hiring process, and with your authorization, [Company] obtained a background check report about you from [Vendor name]. Based on information in that report, [Company] has made a preliminary decision to withdraw its conditional offer of employment. This decision is not final.
[California and other fair-chance jurisdictions:] The conviction(s) that are the basis for this preliminary decision are: [list]. [Optional: a copy of our individualized assessment is enclosed.]

Enclosed are a copy of the report and 'A Summary of Your Rights Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act'. You have [5] business days from receiving this letter to respond before we make a final decision. You may tell us, in writing or by contacting [name, email, phone], if you believe the report is inaccurate or incomplete, and you may send any information you would like us to consider, including evidence of rehabilitation or mitigating circumstances.

[California:] If, within those 5 business days, you tell us that you dispute the accuracy of the report and are taking specific steps to obtain evidence supporting that, you will have at least 5 additional business days to respond.

You may also dispute the accuracy or completeness of the report directly with [Vendor name] at [contact details]. No final decision will be made before the response period ends. [Seattle: we will hold the position open while you respond, as SMC 14.17 requires (verify period).]

sections.title: Final adverse action notice
sections.intro: Sent only after the response period has ended and any response has been reviewed and documented.

items.text: Dear [Candidate name], on [date] we sent you notice of our preliminary decision to withdraw your conditional offer of employment for the [Job title] position, with a copy of your background check report. [We reviewed the information you provided on [date].] [Company] has now made a final decision to withdraw the offer. This decision was based in whole or in part on information in the consumer report provided by [Vendor name].

[Vendor name] did not make this decision and cannot explain why it was made. You have the right to obtain a free copy of your report from [Vendor name] if you ask within 60 days of receiving this notice, and to dispute with [Vendor name] the accuracy or completeness of any information in the report. [Vendor name], [address], [toll-free phone], [website].

[California and fair-chance jurisdictions:] The conviction(s) that were the basis for this decision are: [list]. [Any procedure [Company] has for you to challenge the decision or ask for reconsideration: [describe].] You have the right to file a complaint with the California Civil Rights Department at calcivilrights.ca.gov.
[If a credit score was used:] Your credit score was [score] (possible range [x]-[y]), obtained on [date] from [source]. The key factors that adversely affected the score were: [factors].
items.detail: Credit-score disclosure under 15 U.S.C. 1681m(a)(2). Credit reports only for roles where state law allows them.

items.text: If you have questions, please contact [name, title, email]. We appreciate your interest in [Company].

sections.title: Timeline checklist
sections.intro: Greenhouse tasks mirror these steps; a notice sent out of order is a reportable control failure (TA-05 C2).

items.text: Conditional offer accepted; disclosure, authorization and any state forms (e.g., ICRAA on a separate page) sent through the vendor portal.
Signed authorization received before the report is ordered; order placed within 1 business day of signature.
Report reviewed by TA Operations: clear reports released to People Ops; any record, discrepancy or unverifiable item routed to Legal. Nothing is decided automatically.
Individualized assessment completed and signed by Legal before any notice is sent.
items.when: Within 2 business days of the report

items.text: Pre-adverse notice sent with the report and the Summary of Rights by tracked email (and by mail if the candidate asks); the date of receipt is recorded.

Response window counted in business days from receipt (add 5 days if sent only by mail): at least 5 business days, plus at least 5 more in California if the candidate disputes the report and is getting evidence.
Any response and new evidence reviewed; the final decision and reasons documented by Legal.

Final notice sent, or clearance recorded and the start date released. The file (consent, report, assessment, notices, response) is kept outside the personnel file for at least 4 years for California and at least 1 year elsewhere, and longer under a legal hold.

sections.title: State and city variations
sections.intro: Apply the rules for the work location, and for remote roles the employee's home state.

items.text: California: separate ICRAA disclosure with a copy box; Fair Chance Act (5+ employees) with no criminal inquiry before a conditional offer, a written individualized assessment, 5 + 5 business days and CRD language in the final notice (Gov Code 12952; 2 CCR 11017.1); credit reports only for LC 1024.5 roles such as access to trade secrets or $10,000+ in cash; no questions about cannabis use (Gov Code 12954). Los Angeles and San Francisco ordinances add notice and posting steps (verify for each work location).

Colorado: no criminal-history questions on the initial application or in ads (Chance to Compete Act, C.R.S. 8-2-130), no questions about sealed records, and credit reports only where substantially related to the job, with written disclosure if used in the decision (C.R.S. 8-2-126). Collect date of birth only after the initial application (JAFA).

Washington: from 1 July 2026 (15+ employees), no criminal-history inquiry until the applicant is otherwise qualified and has a conditional offer, no blanket exclusions, and before adverse action identify the record, allow time to respond and document the legitimate business reason (RCW 49.94). Seattle roles also follow SMC 14.17, and credit reports need a substantially job-related reason disclosed in writing (RCW 19.182.020).

Texas: FCRA only. Texas consumer reporting agencies may not report arrests or convictions more than 7 years old unless the salary is $75,000 or more (Bus. & Com. Code 20.05), which matters for interns and technicians. Austin's fair-chance ordinance is treated as preempted (HB 2127), so the company's post-offer standard applies.

North Carolina: no private-sector ban-the-box law, but never ask about or use expunged records (G.S. 15A-153; up to $500 per violation after an NCDOL warning), and have the vendor screen them out. Applicant drug-test positives must be confirmed by GC/MS at an approved lab before an offer is withdrawn (G.S. 95-232).

Other US locations: NYC (Fair Chance Act process with the Fair Chance Notice and Article 23-A analysis), Illinois (IHRA 2-103.1 preliminary notice and 5 business days) and other cities and states add steps. TA Operations keeps the location matrix current in the vendor portal.
These forms are not used outside the US. Each country's limits are in the country notes, and the vendor runs only the checks on Legal's screening matrix for that country and role.

notes: FCRA procedure drives most background-check class actions: a disclosure with one extra sentence, a missing Summary of Rights or a final notice sent on the same day as the pre-adverse notice can each bring statutory damages of $100-$1,000 per applicant for willful violations.
Always two steps: the pre-adverse notice, with the report, must reach the candidate before the decision is final, and the final notice goes only after the response window closes.

The individualized assessment is the company standard in every US state, not just California: Washington also requires it, and it is the approach the EEOC's 2012 arrest-and-conviction guidance recommends under Title VII.
Order only the checks on Legal's screening matrix for the role and location; a vendor 'full package' can break California's credit limits, Texas's 7-year rule and Colorado's credit rules.
Keep consent forms, reports, assessments and notices in the restricted screening file, never in the personnel file or in the hiring team's view in Greenhouse.
Version the templates: the CFPB updates the Summary of Rights and state forms change, so TA Operations reviews them with the vendor every year.

countryNotes.us: The FCRA requires a stand-alone disclosure and written authorization before a report is ordered, a pre-adverse action notice with the report and Summary of Rights, a reasonable wait (commonly 5 business days) and a final adverse action notice (15 U.S.C. 1681b(b), 1681m). Fair-chance laws in NYC, Illinois, Washington, California and elsewhere delay criminal inquiries until after a conditional offer.
countryNotes.us-ca: Add the separate ICRAA disclosure and copy box, follow the Fair Chance Act (written individualized assessment, 5 + 5 business days, CRD rights in the final notice), limit credit checks to LC 1024.5 roles and keep the file 4 years. Never consider cannabis use, arrests without conviction, diversion or sealed records.
countryNotes.us-co: No criminal-history questions on initial applications (C.R.S. 8-2-130), no sealed records, credit reports only where substantially job-related with written disclosure (C.R.S. 8-2-126), and no date of birth on initial applications (JAFA). Otherwise the FCRA steps apply.
countryNotes.us-nc: The FCRA governs and there is no private-sector ban-the-box, but expunged records must never be requested or used (G.S. 15A-153), and drug-test positives must be confirmed before an offer is withdrawn (G.S. 95-232).
countryNotes.us-tx: FCRA only; Texas agencies can't report convictions older than 7 years unless the salary is $75,000+ (Bus. & Com. Code 20.05). Austin's fair-chance ordinance is treated as preempted, so the company's post-offer standard governs.
countryNotes.us-wa: From 1 July 2026, employers with 15+ employees may make criminal inquiries only after a conditional offer, with no blanket exclusions and a documented legitimate business reason after the applicant has had a chance to respond (RCW 49.94); Seattle adds SMC 14.17. Credit reports only where substantially job-related (RCW 19.182.020).
countryNotes.ca: The FCRA forms don't apply. Get written consent and show a legitimate job requirement for criminal and credit checks, give the Ontario Consumer Reporting Act notice where an agency is used, and have the candidate obtain any police check; record of offences (Ontario) and unrelated convictions (BC) are protected grounds.
countryNotes.de: Checks are limited to what the role needs: a certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis) only for trust-sensitive roles, supplied by the candidate, and no credit or deep social-media checks. Standard screening questionnaires need works council consent (§94 BetrVG), and results are deleted once the decision is made.
countryNotes.il: Employers may not ask candidates for a police record extract unless a law authorizes it for the role (Criminal Register and Rehabilitation of Offenders Law 1981), and genetic tests are banned. Verify education and employment with consent, and give candidates their screening results on request.
countryNotes.in: Use written BGV consent covering education, employment, address and criminal checks through court records or police verification. Aadhaar must be voluntary and masked, and original certificates are returned the same day (Karnataka); keep consent even where DPDP s.7(i) may apply.
countryNotes.tw: Criminal records and health data are sensitive under the PDPA and need written consent or a statutory basis. Checks must be job-related and proportionate, and pre-employment medical results are handled as sensitive data.
countryNotes.cn: Private employers can't obtain official criminal-record checks, so rely on candidate declarations and permitted vendor verification under a PIPL notice, separate consent and entrusted-processing agreements. Collect the prior employer's termination certificate; pre-employment medicals may not test for hepatitis B or pregnancy.
countryNotes.vn: Employers can't pull criminal records. Ask the candidate for a Judicial Record Certificate No. 1 only where the role justifies it, with separate consent because the data is sensitive (Decree 356/2025), verify degrees and employment with consent, and never keep original documents.
